On Statecraft, host Geeta Mohan tracks major geopolitical developments shaping global power and elections. In Israel, Central Elections Committee Chief Justice Noam Solberg has directed Shin Bet to probe allegations of foreign funding and electoral interference following claims by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu amid a parliamentary deadlock. Netanyahu's bloc remains short of the 61 seats needed for a majority, leaving Arab parties with potential kingmaker influence. Meanwhile, academic Professor Haim Bresheeth Zabner critiques Israeli politics and voter polarization. Across the Atlantic, President Donald Trump confronts growing challenges ahead of the midterms as Indian American voters reconsider support amid visa restrictions, inflation, and immigration rhetoric, even as Trump backs Vivek Ramaswamy in Ohio. Additionally, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh offered Indian counterterrorism expertise and reiterated regional maritime security commitments at the ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus in the Philippines. Oppn’s SIR Showdown, BJP Counter-Rally & SC Push for Bank Accountability in Digital Arrest Fraud
On News Track with Maria Shakeel, the focus turns to escalating political tensions in Delhi as the INDIA bloc gears up for a public impeachment against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, followed by a mega rally at Ramlila Maidan. In response, the Bharatiya Janata Party has mounted a counter-campaign titled 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao'. The opposition accuses the Election Commission of bias and disenfranchisement through the Special Intensive Revision process, while the ruling party defends the poll body's sworn affidavit submitted before the Supreme Court. Political analysts and party spokespersons examine whether taking protests to the streets undermines institutional decorum or represents a vital democratic fight for accountability. Additionally, the programme covers the Supreme Court taking suo moto cognizance of digital arrest frauds, proposing that banks face prosecution and compensate victims when transactions deviate from normal patterns due to failures in due diligence.
Jamia Students End Hunger Strike; Union Polls In August 2027, Disciplinary Notices Revoked
Students at Jamia Millia Islamia have called off their indefinite hunger strike after university authorities agreed to key demands, ending an 18-day campus agitation. The university administration confirmed that Students' Union elections will be held by the last week of August 2027, marking the resumption of student union polling after two decades. The union constitution is scheduled to be implemented by 15 May, with elections following within six weeks of the new academic session. Authorities also announced the revocation of show cause notices, disciplinary proceedings, suspensions, and campus bans related to the protests. Offline physical classes and examinations will resume following the festive break, restoring academic operations across the university campus.
Israel Election Ends in Stalemate: Netanyahu Bloc Wins 53 Seats, Falls Short of Majority
Counting of votes in the Israeli parliamentary elections has concluded with no political alliance securing a clear majority in the Knesset. The Benjamin Netanyahu-led bloc won 53 seats, remaining eight seats short of the 61-seat threshold required to form a government. The alliance led by Gadi Eisenkot secured 48 seats, leaving both main groupings dependent on negotiations. Arab parties won 19 seats, including eight seats secured by Ra'am, amid conditional offers of outside support for government formation. Both rival blocs must now enter coalition discussions to resolve the parliamentary deadlock following the October 27 voting.
BJP vs Congress: Street Protests, Mock Parliament & The Battle Over the Election Commission
A heated broadcast examines the intensifying confrontation between the ruling BJP and the opposition over street protests, the proposed mock parliament, and allegations regarding the Chief Election Commissioner. BJP National Spokesperson Sanju Verma defends her party's counter-demonstrations, arguing that constitutional rights under Article 19 are accessible to all sides to set the political narrative responsibly. Sanju Verma asserts that if the ruling party exercises these rights 'judiciously' and 'with restraint to prove a point', there should be no criticism. Meanwhile, Congress representative Adil Singh Bhoparai criticises democratic institutions as compromised, justifying novel protest tactics including a symbolic impeachment. Senior journalist Swati Chaturvedi calls the concept of a mock parliament juvenile and cautions that personalised attacks detract from systemic issues. Political analyst Sajjan Kumar highlights an unprecedented dynamic where both the ruling party and the opposition hit the streets simultaneously, overshadowing conventional legislative debate and signalling deeper institutional standoffs.
